PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL - ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
MEMORANDUM: Redline Review - Harland PERS Markup of Crestline IAA (received 4/8/25; $350M Large Cap Core SMA)
To: J. Halperin. Due 4/14; call 4/15; response 4/21. Never share playbook floors externally.

1. BOTTOM LINE
Three true deal-breakers: (A) Sec. 18 sovereign-immunity structure; (B) Sec. 15(e) FOIA no-notice; (C) Sec. 6(d) MFN as drafted. Four more are Reject-as-drafted but solvable: Sec. 11(c) 180-day/Board-approval exit; Sec. 13(b) Thornton "substantially all time"; Sec. 9 liability/indemnity/consequential/liquidated damages; Sec. 11(b)(iv),(vi) performance/reputational "Cause". Soft dollars (8(b)) is Negotiate, and less severe than the playbook assumes. Accept (minor edits): fee tiers (at pre-authorized floor), SOC 1, pay-to-play, brokerage reporting, proxy retention. Critical: the redline is not a clean markup of our 3/14 form (Part 9). Whitford's possible $500M increase justifies flexibility on compromisable items.

2. A. SOVEREIGN IMMUNITY (Sec. 18(a)-(d), Preamble) - REJECT as drafted; deal-breaker; fix via limited waiver
- 18(b) has Client "consent" to Harland County courts and Adviser's irrevocable immunity waiver; 18(c) ("notwithstanding any other provision") reserves all Client immunity including the Eleventh Amendment. 18(c) overrides Client's consent, leaving Adviser bound and Client not.
- Law (from memory; sources unreachable; unverified): Eleventh Amendment/Hans v. Louisiana bars unconsented private suits against a State in federal court if Client is an "arm of the State" (Regents v. Doe, 519 U.S. 425 (1997); Hess v. Port Authority, 513 U.S. 30 (1994): state-treasury exposure is the key factor; pension systems are mixed, fact-specific). Alden v. Maine, 527 U.S. 706 (1999), preserves state immunity in the State's own courts, so exclusive Harland courts do not solve it; Harland law and any contract-claims/waiver statute control. Waiver must be express and unequivocal (Edelman v. Jordan; College Savings Bank v. Florida Prepaid, 527 U.S. 666 (1999); Lapides, 535 U.S. 613 (2002)); an official lacking statutory authority cannot waive, which is Voss's point.
- Conclusion: as drafted the contract is functionally unenforceable against Client in federal court and unenforceable in state court unless a Harland statute waives immunity for contract claims (unverified; not in file). That is exactly the termination-quarter fee scenario Sarah described. Change #1 ("instrumentality...established pursuant to the laws") bolsters arm-of-state status.
- The redline silently dropped Client's standard-form rep (Std. 7(b)(ii)) that the Agreement is legal, valid, binding and enforceable against it.
- Counter: (1) restore AAA arbitration (Harland law acceptable per playbook if arbitration stays; neutral/Harland venue fine); (2) Client waiver, to the extent permitted by Harland law, for claims for fees and Client breach, with Client rep of authority and enforceability and a Harland AG/Client counsel opinion; (3) delete Adviser waiver or make mutual; (4) payment self-help: standing, irrevocable instruction to Northern Ridge to debit fees from the Account (ADV Item 5 already permits; 6(c) is merely permissive), including a final-quarter debit before transfer-out; (5) fallback if litigation insisted: mutual jurisdiction, jury waiver, mutual fees (playbook). 18(d) mutual prevailing-party fees: Accept only once immunity is reciprocal (Std. 18(d): own fees).

3. B. CONFIDENTIALITY/FOIA (15(e), 15(f)) - REJECT 15(e); NEGOTIATE 15(f)
- 15(e) deletes 10-business-day notice (Std. 15(c)(v)) and lets Client disclose "any and all" information, including process descriptions, "required or permitted", with no liability. Playbook: non-negotiable; ask 10 business days, floor 5.
- Voss cites AG Opinion 2022-14 (notice clauses unenforceable against instrumentalities); not supplied; obtain (AG opinions typically persuasive only; unverified). If correct, offer a substitute: (i) Adviser marks trade secrets/methodology/trade-level data; Client treats as exempt to the fullest extent of Harland FOIA and asserts trade-secret exemptions; (ii) notice "as soon as practicable and at least 5 business days where law permits, otherwise upon receipt"; (iv) delete "or permitted" and "without liability"; (v) disclose only fees, performance, relationship; show trade-level data/models by presentation, leaving no copies.
- Restore silently dropped trade-secret survival (Std. 15(f)) and the "terms of agreement" confidentiality; 5-year survival is an available give (playbook).
- 15(f): the text is not an "absolute prohibition even with consent" as the email states; consent remains but in Client's "sole and absolute discretion", barred for oral use. Counter: consent not unreasonably withheld for RFP/DDQ, consultants, regulatory filings (Std. 15(d)).

4. C. FEES AND MFN (6(a), 6(b), 6(d), Ex. A)
- Tiers 42/32/22 equal the floor Thornton pre-authorized (3 bps). ACCEPT. $350M: $1,370,000 vs $1,475,000 = -$105,000 (7.12%) per year; -$315,000 over the 3-year term; at $500M $1,850,000 vs $2,000,000 = -$150,000 (7.5%). No further fee authority exists; anything lower, including via MFN, needs Thornton.
- 6(b) end-of-quarter value: playbook-acceptable but fix: (i) value on date before any withdrawal; (ii) partial/termination quarter valued at termination date (as drafted, liquidating before quarter-end could zero the final-quarter fee); (iii) adjust for large flows.
- 6(d) MFN: Reject as drafted. Defects vs playbook 3.6: no service-level or vehicle definition; any tier (cherry-picking) rather than blended; comparator $200M+ rather than +/-25% of Client ($262.5M-$437.5M); no 2 bp materiality threshold; retroactive refund to the other client's start date; rep that no existing public plan pays less (retroactive in effect; audit existing Large Cap Core fees before any rep); 10-business-day notice (playbook 30 calendar days); survival. Each 1 bp across tiers = $35,000/yr at $350M, $50,000 at $500M. Counter with the playbook package (SMA-to-SMA, comparable service, prospective only, +/-25%, 2 bp, blended rate, GC certification; no audit; fee data of other clients stays confidential). MFN could pierce the floor: Thornton sign-off.

5. D. SOFT DOLLARS (8(a), 8(b)) - NEGOTIATE (not outright Reject)
- ADV Item 12 already offers client opt-out to execution-only (commissions $0.01-0.02/share vs $0.03-0.05); the playbook's "execution-only = lowest price ignoring all else" misreads what we disclose, so 8(b) is consistent with ADV.
- Economics: $1.8M firm-wide soft dollars; 8.33% share = ~$150,000/yr = 10.17% of standard fee, 10.95% of $1,370,000. Caveat: research is funded by participating accounts' commissions, so true hard-dollar cost may be lower. Combined with the fee cut, concessions total ~$255,000/yr (17.3% of $1,475,000).
- Counter: accept execution-only/no 28(e) usage for the Account; define permitted commission arrangements to exclude execution-related services; delete "solely" and "each transaction most favorable... best efforts" in 8(a) (not in our form; conflicts with best-execution case law) ; trade it for the floor and a narrowed MFN; any RPA/fee adjustment needs Thornton approval.

6. E. KEY PERSON AND CHANGE OF CONTROL (1, 11(b)(v), 13)
- 13(b): REJECT Thornton as drafted. "Substantially all" time is impossible: he manages all four strategies ($4.2B; ADV Item 10; Best Execution Committee, Item 12), so signing would be an immediate breach. Counter: Marchetti only; "meaningful professional time and attention consistent with role"; if Thornton must appear, "continued executive oversight"; notice 10 business days (not 5); Client termination right on 30 days (acceptable), exercisable within a window; replacement not in Client's "sole discretion"; delete "leave of absence >30 days" and duplicate 11(b)(v) Cause trigger.
- 13(a): REJECT 25%/"any change in identity of controlling person"/sixty-day pre-closing consent. Playbook: floor 50% or a functional control test, 30-60 days' notice, post-change Client termination right; carve out employee equity grants, ownership-plan and internal transfers (ADV Item 10 discloses minority grants to key professionals). Caveat: the playbook's "SEC 50%" rationale is unverified; Investment Company Act s.2(a)(9) presumes control above 25% (unverified), so 25% is not arbitrary; rely on the functional test (Advisers Act s.202(a)(1); Rule 202(a)(1)-1: no change of actual control/management, no assignment; unverified). Playbook text/table conflict on functional test; GC to confirm.

7. F. LIABILITY (9, 24, 14(c))
- 9(a): Playbook says Reject removal of "breach of fiduciary duty". Facially pro-Adviser, but paired with 14(c) ("highest fiduciary duty"), the retained "violation of Applicable Law" carve-out (Applicable Law now includes the unseen Harland Act) and Sec. 24 third-party beneficiary rights; net effect is fault-free statutory liability. Restore standard text; fiduciary acknowledgment under Advisers Act and Harland law acceptable (playbook); Act compliance only for identified provisions after Kessler review; delete Sec. 24 beneficiary insert (Std. 22).
- 9(b): REJECT negligence-triggered, "defend", one-sided indemnity. Restore mutual standard; cap both sides at 12 months' fees.
- 9(c): REJECT. One-sided; drafting inverted ("Adviser shall not be liable... arising from Adviser's claims"). Counter: mutual; fallback cap at 12 months' fees ($1.37M). Uncapped consequential claims on a $350M account (a 5% loss = $17.5M) exceed E&O $10M/occurrence.
- 9(d): NEGOTIATE. 1.5x quarterly fee = $513,750 at floor ($553,125 standard; $693,750 at $500M) per "transaction", cumulative with actual damages, triggered by passive breaches: penalty risk (Truck Rent-A-Center v. Puritan Farms 2nd, 41 N.Y.2d 420 (1977); Restatement (Second) Contracts s.356; Harland law unknown). Counter: replace with make-whole trade-error remedy; if retained: knowing breaches of hard restrictions, exclusive, capped, credited.

8. G. TERMINATION AND CAUSE (11)
- 11(b) 30 days Client vs 11(c) 180 days plus Board approval: REJECT. Playbook minimum 60 days mutual; asymmetry, Board approval, and >120 days are must-rejects; Board approval makes Adviser's exit discretionary. Counter: mutual 60 days; if needed Client 60/Adviser 90, courtesy Board notice, transition cooperation (11(d), acceptable).
- Cause: (iv) two-quarter performance trigger REJECT: with +/-200 bp tracking error, net-of-fee underperformance in two straight quarters is roughly a 1-in-4 event even for a zero-alpha manager, and Client already has 60/30-day no-cause exit. Playbook's s.205(a)(1) rationale is weak; lead with other grounds; offer a performance-review meeting after trailing 3-year underperformance. (vi) reputational event in Client's discretion REJECT. (v) Key Person as Cause REJECT (duplicative). (vii) "cause under Applicable Law" undefined: delete. Accept fraud, felony, guideline breach with cure (playbook).

9. H. UNMARKED/UNLISTED DEVIATIONS AND DOCUMENT RED FLAGS
- The 37-item Appendix omits: Sec. 24; "Strategy" definition incorporating our 11/15/24 RFP response (delete; conflicts with Sec. 21); 10(a)(ix) RFP-accuracy rep ("complete"; qualify); "continuing basis" reps; Applicable Law definition; Board signature block; Sec. 19 copy.
- Redline "deleted" text does not match our form (9(a)-(c), 11(b)); unmarked variances: Sec. 17 adds CGL $5M, $10M fidelity bond and 2-year E&O tail (Std. 14(a): none; check with broker); non-renewal notice 60 vs 90 days; 5-day best-efforts cure vs Std. 10 business days (playbook allows 5; use "commercially reasonable"); lost 9(a) market/custodian/force-majeure exclusions and 9(d) defense-control; lost Client reps (Std. 7(b)); IPS cash cap 5% and divestment list in Ex. B (IPS not yet delivered; require before signing).
- Notice email is wrong (crestlinecap.com vs crestlinecapital.com); notice deemed on sending, not receipt. Machine-compare to 3/14 form before responding.
- Effective Date June 1, 2025 is a Sunday and mid-quarter (not "first business day of the quarter"); make it the later of June 1 and Board approval (5/22) plus execution and IPS delivery. Recital says $500M increase "subject to Board approval"; Appendix #4 says "board-approved": non-binding; clarify no funding commitment (Std. 1(c) already has an option).
- Playbook lists different strategies from ADV Item 5 (relevant to MFN "same strategy"); ADV dated 3/31/25 says no changes since 3/29/24 (confirm 2025 annual amendment filed; ADV Item 9 not supplied, needed before the 10(a)(vi) five-year clean-record rep).

10. I. REMAINING ITEMS
- ACCEPT: 14(f) SOC 1 (Pennfield) but delete Client approval of auditor; 8(d) brokerage reports (soften best-execution certification); 12 seven-year retention; 16 proxy retention (playbook; make 10-day contested notice "5 business days or as practicable", Adviser recommendation only when delegated); 14(d) pay-to-play: facts confirmed (ADV Item 14; no placement agent; Std. 7(a)(vii) already had it), but align (ii) to Rule 206(4)-5 "covered associates", two-year look-back and de minimis exceptions (unverified), not "any employee... any political subdivision".
- NEGOTIATE: 3/Ex. B approved-securities list (must be asset-class/negative-list level; trade pre-approval is playbook must-reject); 4 unilateral IPS amendment REJECT (mutual; legal divestments with implementation period and impracticability remedy beyond "good faith"); 5 custodian change (qualified custodian, operational compatibility); 7(a),(b) monthly narrative to quarterly, certificate by CCO not PM; 8(e) broker list (quarterly update, Adviser may add, no retroactive removal); 14(e) Inspector General: scope to Account records, annual, 30 days' notice, business hours, confidentiality, privilege preserved (verify the "cannot be modified" claim in the Act); 10(a)(vi)-(viii) reps with knowledge qualifiers.

11. NEXT STEPS
Obtain Harland Act, FOIA, AG Op. 2022-14, immunity statute, IPS; engage Harland counsel; Thornton approvals (MFN, soft-dollar trade); fee audit for MFN rep; broker/insurance check; response letter to Voss in neutral, board-readable tone, with package proposal; walk through on 4/15.
